transcript:
Header: 2025-05-14 15:00 PDT / Duration: 42 mins / Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (CTO - Arcadia), Priya Rao (Lead Engineer - Arcadia), Sam Ortiz (PM - Arcadia)

Summary: sync on POC integration, focus on SDK examples for function/tool calling and generating stable structured JSON output for downstream ingestion.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check in, how's the integration work been going on your side?
00:12 Liam: Hey Maya, yeah, been okay. Priya's been plumbin the SDK into our staging service, we hit some weird partial JSON returns though so wanted to talk about schema enforcement.
00:25 Priya: yah, the function-calling flow works but sometimes the model returns text that veers off, like extra commentary before the JSON block, so our parser chokes.
00:38 Jonah: got it. Two levers we typically use — one is stricter function schemas in the SDK call, and the other is a post-parse fallback that can salvage near-miss JSON. i'll send a snippet. also check prompt anchors so the model knows to only return the object.
01:02 Sam: can you clarify what you mean by function-schema? is that the typed signature we've seen in the docs?
01:10 Jonah: yeah so in the SDK you declare functions with field types and required fields. the runtime will prefer that format when doing tool calls; if the model attempts free text we get schema mismatch warnings. note transcription: sometimes our docs show Redwooed instead of Redwood.
01:30 Priya: we've got the schema declared but the SDK example in our code is slightly older. could you send an updated snippet with the "required" fields? also examples for nested arrays.
01:45 Maya: absolutely. i'll attach an updated snippet. also include an example where we call an external tool — like a DB write or an internal search — from the function call.
01:58 Jonah: quick note about logs: when a function call is invoked the SDK emits a call trace and the structured response; you can configure to persist those for debugging. do you want us to enable more verbose tracing for the pilot?
02:12 Liam: yes please, we'll need traces for the first 1000 requests. cost wise how much extra logging impacts us?
02:20 Jonah: trace logs are small relative to token cost, but there's storage and retention variables. we'll include a verbose setting you can toggle.
02:34 Priya: another issue: occasionally there's a blank "arguments" field returned. is that a timeout or a kv cache issue?
02:45 Jonah: could be a couple things — either an early cut because of token limits, or the runtime fell back during heavy load, or a KV cache hydration problem. we saw similar behavior in earlier tests. can you share the failing traces?
02:59 Priya: yes we'll collect them. also latency is a concern — real-time features expect sub-300ms tail p99 for short prompts. can Dedicated help?
03:12 Maya: Dedicated gives more predictable p99s, but it depends on model size and quantization. Hosted can hit sub-300ms for smaller models but burstiness can cause variance. we should schedule a bench.
03:27 Jonah: for the bench i'll need your typical prompt length, concurrency, and whether you use embeddings in the pipeline. that'll drive batching vs single-request tuning.
03:41 Sam: our typical prompt is ~220 tokens, sometimes we call the search tool first and then do function call. concurrency expected around 40 qps for the pilot.
03:55 Jonah: okay 220 tokens and 40 qps is useful. i'll sketch options: 1) hosted with continuous batching and cache for prefix yields low cost but variable p99; 2) Dedicated pinned instances for stable p99 with slightly higher committed cost; 3) hybrid routing: route mission-critical requests to Dedicated and less critical to hosted.
04:22 Liam: what about private deployment? we have some PHI concerns.
04:26 Maya: Private (VPC/on-prem) is available but has longer lead time. for pilot you can run hosted with encryption and SOC2 controls, plus we can enable customer-managed KMS if needed. we'll share the security pack.
04:45 Priya: perfect. about the partial JSON — could we enforce a wrapper token like "BEGIN_JSON...END_JSON" and then parse between? is that supported?
04:58 Jonah: you can do that at prompt level, but function schemas tend to be more robust. we also recommend a small regex sanitizer and a retry policy: if parsing fails, call the model with a very strict instruction set to only return the JSON.
05:20 Sam: any examples of prompt templating for that?
05:24 Jonah: yes i'll include a few: one with system instruction + function schema, one with wrapper tokens, and one with a two-step approach: generate then validate.
05:38 Priya: regarding SDK behavior, what's the client-side timeout default? we saw a 10s default that sometimes cuts off long generation.
05:47 Maya: default is 10s for long-poll; you can set per-call timeout or use streaming to start processing earlier. for function calls streaming is supported but you sometimes have to buffer until the function name + args are complete.
06:05 Liam: on model variants — if we need smaller model for latency is there a quality regression monitoring?
06:12 Jonah: yes Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and model variants and we can hook quality monitors against your eval set. for pilot we can configure regression alerts on a per-prompt set.
06:28 Priya: can we get the SDK in TypeScript? our stack is node.
06:33 Maya: yes we have official JS/TS SDK. i'll include an idiomatic example showing function definitions and the typed responses for structured outputs.
06:44 Sam: are there any gotchas with JSON schema enforcement and arrays of objects? we had mismatch errors with extra fields in the past.
06:52 Jonah: mark unknown fields as additionalProperties=false if you want strict validation, or allow them and post-validate. our SDK emits schema mismatch warnings in the logs so you can tune.
07:06 Priya: great. one more thing: telemetry — can we tag requests by customer feature flag or tenant id so we can slice metrics?
07:14 Maya: yep, metadata headers are supported. include x-arcadia-tenant and we'll route those into per-tenant dashboards.
07:22 Liam: ok next steps and deliverables?
07:25 Maya: i'll send the code snippets and the security docs. Jonah will set up a bench plan. Priya will run integration and collect failing traces. we'll meet next week same time.
07:36 Sam: also please include an example webhook pattern for tool-calls where the model triggers a downstream async job, we want idempotency guidance.
07:46 Jonah: i'll add a short note: always include a request_id and function invocation id, and favor at-least-once semantics with de-dup keys.
07:58 Priya: thanks. we'll also validate PII fields and redaction; Liam will confirm which fields are sensitive.
08:06 Liam: yes i'll confirm within 48 hours.
08:11 Maya: excellent, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in writing with the artifacts.
08:16 (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains transcription artifacts ("kay vee cache" for KV cache, occasional speaker mislabels). References: deck link: https://redwood.ai/poc/arcadia-deck (shared), bench spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/bench/arcadia (private link).
